title: arXiv Physics — Daily (2026-10-23 announcement batch)
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not an official arXiv trending chart. arXiv supplies no official readership or trend ranking, and citation evidence for papers this recent is limited; ordering relies on checkable publication, data-release, cross-field, facility, and concrete-result signals rather than measured popularity.
ranking_context: Semantic Scholar citation fields were not sufficiently available for this snapshot; citation counts and age-normalized citation momentum are not claimed.

sections.title: Lifetime of the singly charged 229Th nuclear isomer
sections.authors: Y. Shigekawa, A. Yamaguchi, K. Tokoi, N. Sato, H. Kikunaga, et al.
sections.abstract: The authors produce 229mTh+ in an ion trap and measure a 0.46(8) s half-life, which they interpret as indirect evidence for electronic-bridge decay.
sections.claimed_result: The authors determine a 229mTh+ half-life of 0.46(8) s from ion-trap and internal-conversion-electron measurements; the unexpectedly fast decay suggests, but does not directly establish, electronic-bridge decay.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; charge-exchange production in an ion trap and time-dependent ion/electron counts.
sections.unique_caveat: The electronic-bridge channel is inferred from the lifetime rather than directly identified; calculations of the relevant electronic states and decay rates remain uncertain.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between nuclear and atomic physics; the arXiv record links a Nature Physics journal reference and DOI, corroborating the result's publication status.

sections.title: QUIJOTE scientific results - XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
sections.authors: F. Vansyngel, J. A. Rubino-Martin, P. de Ferra, R. B. Barreiro, R. T. Genova-Santos, et al.
sections.abstract: Combining QUIJOTE-MFI wide-survey maps with Planck and WMAP, the authors measure polarized Galactic synchrotron power spectra and estimate its contribution to future CMB B-mode measurements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find EE and BB spectra consistent with power laws over 30<ell<130, estimate a synchrotron BB/EE ratio near 0.2, and infer foreground levels equivalent to approximately r=0.003 at 90 GHz and r=0.0002 at 150 GHz for the analysed masks and scales.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; QUIJOTE-MFI 10–20 GHz wide survey combined with Planck and WMAP maps.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimate is limited to selected sky masks and multipoles; the possible EE/BB slope difference is only about 1.6 sigma, and no spatial variation in the synchrotron spectral index is resolved within current uncertainties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for publication in MNRAS; combines an observing-survey release with Planck and WMAP data on a key foreground for primordial B-mode searches.

sections.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
sections.authors: Qiaoyang Hao, Tao Wang, Weishan Zhu, Hong Guo, Peng Wang, et al.
sections.abstract: The authors use COSMOS-Web DR1 and simulation-calibrated probabilistic redshift slices to construct and release a high-redshift cosmic-filament catalog and probability maps.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 12,523 filaments and 136,210 segments over 0.5<z<3.5, extracted from COSMOS-Web DR1 using photometric-redshift probability realizations and thresholds optimized on TNG simulation mocks.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and computational; COSMOS-Web DR1 galaxy data, DisPerSE-based extraction, and TNG mock-catalog calibration.
sections.unique_caveat: The structures are inferred from projected tomographic slices, so photometric-redshift errors and projection effects remain; the parameter calibration also depends on the chosen simulation mocks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across cosmology, galaxy astrophysics, and instrumentation/methods; releases filament and segment catalogs plus probability maps, and the record links an A&A DOI.

sections.title: Search for Ultra-Relativistic Magnetic Monopoles with LHAASO-KM2A
sections.authors: Zhen Cao, F. Aharonian, Y. X. Bai, Y. W. Bao, D. Bastieri, et al.
sections.abstract: Using 1,438.81 live days of LHAASO-KM2A observations, the collaboration searches for ultra-relativistic magnetic monopoles and reports flux upper limits rather than a detection.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no statistically significant excess and set 90% confidence upper limits from 2.6×10^-16 to 8.8×10^-19 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 for Lorentz factors 10^5 to 10^7.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; LHAASO-KM2A air-shower data and a machine-learning classifier applied to electromagnetic-detector shower-shape observables.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a null search, not evidence of monopoles; the limits depend on simulated signal response, background separation, and detector exposure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large LHAASO-KM2A data set supports a quantitative constraint in a stated Lorentz-factor range, including a flux window the authors describe as previously unconstrained.

sections.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
sections.authors: F. Chen, Z. M. Shen, N. Sun, P. Li, Z. Y. Qiu, et al.
sections.abstract: Combining two radially resolved plasma diagnostics, the authors report evidence that an edge-originating quasi-coherent mode couples to core turbulence and drives forward energy transfer across scales.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret the observed quasi-coherent mode and broadband-turbulence coupling as evidence for net forward transfer from ion to electron scales, with associated secondary instabilities.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; multichannel collective Thomson scattering and radially localized Doppler backscattering in tokamak plasma.
sections.unique_caveat: The transfer mechanism is an interpretation of measured fluctuation coupling; its generality and implications for reactor confinement require tests across discharges and operating conditions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports a concrete experimental result using complementary multichannel scattering diagnostics, addressing cross-scale transport in fusion plasmas.

sections.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
sections.authors: Yaqi Li, Mingyu Tong, Fujia Chen, Li Zhang, Rui Zhao, et al.
sections.abstract: The authors reconstruct a magneto-optical bound state's far-field polarization texture, measure topological charge +1, and show that changing magnetic bias reverses polarization handedness without changing that charge.
sections.claimed_result: From a polarization-resolved angle-dependent reflection matrix, the authors reconstruct a counterclockwise 2π winding (q=+1) and observe reversal of far-field handedness as magnetic bias changes.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; microwave-frequency magneto-optical photonic-crystal slab and polarization-resolved reflection measurements, interpreted with a non-Hermitian coupled-mode model.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiment cannot access the central angular region |theta|<6 degrees; the model-based account of chirality reversal is not itself a direct measurement of modal hybridization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports an experimental topological measurement and a specific polarization-extraction method that avoids assuming reciprocity in a time-reversal-breaking system.

sections.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
sections.authors: L. Bruno, B. Koribalski, R. P. Norris, A. Ivleva, T. Venturi, et al.
sections.abstract: Multi-frequency radio maps of ORC J1555+2726 show spectral features that the authors interpret as shock re-acceleration of an existing relativistic-electron population.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure a radial spectral flattening at the ring and a convex integrated spectrum; they argue these are more consistent with re-acceleration of fossil relativistic electrons than thermal-particle shock acceleration plus standard ageing.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; LOFAR, uGMRT, and MeerKAT imaging and spectral-index analysis from 50–1,284 MHz.
sections.unique_caveat: The fossil-plasma/shock account is an interpretation of radio spectral structure; the authors' comment indicates the manuscript has been resubmitted, not that peer review is complete.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines LOFAR, upgraded GMRT, and MeerKAT observations from 50–1,284 MHz; cross-listed between galaxy astrophysics and cosmology, with a comment noting resubmission to A&A after referee review.

sections.title: FRB 20210601A: Extreme Temporal Clustering in a Repeating Fast Radio Burst Source as Evidence for a Hidden Class of Episodic Repeaters
sections.authors: Ryan Mckinven, Amanda M. Cook, Alice P. Curtin, B. M. Gaensler, Jason W. T. Hessels, et al.
sections.abstract: CHIME/FRB observations reveal a brief burst storm from FRB 20210601A amid years of non-detections, motivating a model of episodically active repeaters and a forecast of their detectable population.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue that the source is consistent with an episodically active repeater population and forecast about 1–4 similar discoveries in the next decade of CHIME/FRB operations.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and computational; CHIME/FRB burst detections and exposure-aware population modelling.
sections.unique_caveat: The population estimate is driven by one unusually active source and is very broad (9+200/-8 sources at 68% credibility); selection effects and future detections could change it substantially.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A measured cluster of at least nine bursts in 106.5 seconds, set against roughly 320 hours of exposure over seven years, offers a sharply defined observational case and a testable population forecast.
